references.text: God's wrath burns against those who provoke him, and he threatens to punish them with the sword and destruction.
God warns that he will bring the sword upon the people as punishment for breaking the covenant.
The prophet describes how widows and orphans are left behind as a result of God's judgment on the people.
God threatens to let children's fathers die by the sword, so that the children become fatherless.
Widows become numerous when God brings judgment and destruction upon the people.
Young men were consumed by fire and the sword, and the widows could not weep over their husbands.
The Lord's wrath burns against the people who complain, and his fire consumes them.
As part of the covenant curses, it is warned that sons and daughters will be taken away.
Both verses illustrate how God's wrath over covenant breaking strikes the whole family with the loss of spouses and children.
Both verses show how God's judgment hands the people over to enemies who destroy the family by taking or killing the children.
Both verses use the unique expression that the Lord's wrath 'flames up,' leading to the destruction of the people.
